o1.biggest_strength: A complete, publishable page in our own voice: the flat-note limit and the snug-first-week slots are stated plainly above the fold, again in 'what fits', and again in the FAQ, so the two return drivers get handled without scaring anyone off. The 'light day / full day / most it takes / what doesn't fit' block is the best thing in either submission for a buyer checking their own carry.
o1.biggest_mistake: It shipped an SEO title at 63 characters when I asked for about 60, and left the break-in reassurance off the line under the add-to-cart button, which is the one spot where it does the most work. Quoting our own review counts at customers ('Of our 400 reviews, 142 say the same thing') reads like a stat sheet, not Bellroy, and '8 cards, a few notes, a few coins... still closes flat' adds coins to the 8-card proof line the data doesn't support.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cut the SEO title under 60, move the break-in note into the add-to-cart line, drop the review tallies in favour of one plain owner quote, and confirm the hidden-pocket capacity so we aren't publishing an unverified number.

o2.biggest_strength: The sharpest read of the returns data: 'about 10 flat notes' and 'slots are snug for a week, then ease' both sit in the line under the add-to-cart button, the 3.3-in-100-orders maths is right, and it spots that the 12% colour returns are a photo problem, not a copy problem. Character counts on the SEO title (48) and meta (146) are accurate to the digit.
o2.biggest_mistake: Opened a 'finished work' delivery with a 160-word internal strategy memo and closed it with a 90-day watch plan. That's an email to me, not product page copy, and I'd have to cut 200 words before the web team could use it. Meanwhile the small coin pouch, one of the trade-offs I explicitly asked to be handled honestly, never made the bullets.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Move the memo and the watch-list into a covering note, promote the coin pouch into a bullet, and add light-day/full-day carry scenarios to 'what fits' so a buyer can see their own pocket in it.

reason: Output 1 is the page I could put on the site this afternoon, with the cash limit and the break-in handled everywhere it matters. Output 2 thinks harder about my returns and writes the better add-to-cart line, but I'd have to cut the strategy memo off the top and add the coin pouch before it ships.
